mainTopic: Carrying and drinking across domains on שבת: רבא's 'over the head' rule, liability for spitting and urinating, רבי יהודה on spittle, and whether the drinking rule applies to a כרמלית.
overview: The amud opens by rejecting רב חיננא's view that the whole משנה follows רבי מאיר: the סיפא is רבי מאיר, but the רישא is רבנן. Next, the גמרא asks whether the משנה's words 'ובלבד שלא יוציא חוץ' support or refute רבא's rule about carrying four אמות over one's head. In both versions, the משנה turns out to be ambiguous, so it proves nothing either way. רב יוסף then rules that urinating or spitting from a רשות היחיד into a רשות הרבים is חייב חטאת, because a person's intent makes even a small spot count as a significant place (מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום). רבא asks whether we follow where the urine is uprooted or where it exits, and the question ends in תיקו. On spitting, a contradiction in רבי יהודה's view is resolved by רבי יוחנן's switch of names in the dried-fig משנה, after ריש לקיש's 'phlegm' answer is refuted. A side teaching warns against spitting phlegm in front of one's רבו. Finally, a new משנה forbids drinking across domains unless one's head and most of his body are inside. רב יוסף explains that even the רבנן agree when the person needs the object. אביי and רבא then dispute whether this applies to a כרמלית, and אביי begins a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the earlier אמורא thought the whole משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reasoning of רב חיננא. Since the סיפא of the משנה follows רבי מאיר, he assumed the רישא does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He held: since the latter clause is רבי מאיר, the first clause is also רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב חיננא, the earlier אמורא, said what he said. His view was that the whole משנה follows one author, רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic assumption that one משנה usually has one author. Since the end of the משנה (the סיפא) clearly matches רבי מאיר, רב חיננא assumed the beginning (the רישא) matches רבי מאיר as well.

keyTerms.meaning: He held / his reasoning was
The latter (ending) clause of a משנה
The first (opening) clause of a משנה
Also / likewise

phrases.english: He (Rav Chinnana) held:
since the latter clause is Rabbi Meir,
the first clause is also Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind an אמורא's position from earlier on the דף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining an אמורא's assumption about who authored the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear why רב חיננא attributed the רישא to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He reasoned that one author wrote the whole משנה, so the סיפא's author also wrote the רישא.

steps.title: Rejecting that assumption: the two clauses have different authors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב חיננא's assumption. The סיפא is רבי מאיר, but the רישא is רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so: the latter clause is רבי מאיר, and the first clause is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רב חיננא's reasoning is wrong. The two halves of the משנה follow different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה can be a combination of opinions. Here the רישא reflects the view of the רבנן, and only the סיפא reflects רבי מאיר. So you cannot use the סיפא to tell you who wrote the רישא.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (the גמרא rejecting a view)
The Sages (the majority opinion)
רבי מאיר, a תנא

steps.whatToRemember: A single משנה can mix opinions: here the רישא is רבנן and the סיפא is רבי מאיר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that every משנה has only one author. The גמרא here explicitly splits it between two opinions.

phrases.english: But that is not so:
the latter clause is Rabbi Meir,
and the first clause is the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning explained in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the רישא and סיפא share the same author
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה is split: the סיפא follows רבי מאיר and the רישא follows רבנן.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's limit and inferring liability
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'ובלבד שלא יוציא חוץ' from the משנה and infers that if he did carry beyond four אמות, he is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Provided that he does not carry it beyond.' This implies that if he did carry it beyond, he is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה and drawing an inference from it. This step sets up the next move: the inference will be tested against רבא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits someone standing in a רשות היחיד to move objects in the רשות הרבים, as long as he does not carry them beyond four אמות. The גמרא reads the opposite side of that condition: if he did go beyond, he must be fully liable, which means a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that / as long as
Beyond (here: beyond four אמות)
This implies (introduces an inference)
Sin-offering, brought for an unintentional Torah-level sin

phrases.english: Provided that he does not carry it beyond (four cubits).
This implies: if he carried it out, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new discussion on a different phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inference from the משנה is that carrying beyond four אמות makes one חייב חטאת.

steps.title: Proposed support for רבא's rule about carrying over one's head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this inference supports רבא. רבא rules that carrying an object four אמות in רשות הרבים is liable even if it passed above one's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רבא? For רבא said: one who moves an object from the start of four אמות to the end of four אמות, and moved it above his head, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the inference from step 3 as proof for a ruling of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that the object's path through the air above a person's head does not break the act of carrying four אמות. In our משנה, the man stands in a raised רשות היחיד and moves objects at that height. If he is still חייב חטאת for going beyond four אמות, that matches רבא: an unusual path does not cancel liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
One who moves (carries) an object along
Four cubits, the distance that makes carrying in רשות הרבים forbidden
Through the air above him (over his head)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic question in הלכות שבת: does the path an object takes, such as through an exempt area overhead, affect liability for carrying four אמות?

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports Rava,
for Rava said:
one who moves an object from the beginning of four (cubits)
to the end of four (cubits),
and moved it over his head, is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 3 as possible support for רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that carrying four אמות 'דרך עליו' is חייב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's implication that going beyond four אמות brings a חטאת

steps.title: Rejecting the support: maybe it is only forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The משנה never says חייב חטאת; perhaps it means פטור אבל אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it actually teach 'if he carried out he is liable to a חטאת'? Perhaps: if he carried out, he is exempt but it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 4. It points out that the משנה's words could be read differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ובלבד שלא יוציא' only tells us not to do it. It does not say what happens if he does. It could mean a rabbinic prohibition, which is פטור אבל אסור, and then it gives no support to רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually teach? (challenging an inference)
Perhaps
Exempt from Torah punishment but rabbinically forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: פטור אבל אסור does not mean the act is allowed. It is still forbidden; there is just no Torah-level חטאת.

phrases.english: Does it teach:
'If he carried out, he is liable to a sin-offering'?
Perhaps if he carried out —
he is exempt but it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָתָנֵי: אִם הוֹצִיא חַיָּיב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רבא from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference of חייב חטאת is not forced; the משנה may mean only פטור אבל אסור.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, the משנה gives no proof for רבא, because it may mean only פטור אבל אסור.

steps.title: Second version: the inference is exempt but forbidden
steps.stepSummary: An alternate version (איכא דאמרי) holds that the גמרא's inference from the משנה was פטור אבל אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: this implies that if he carried out, he is exempt but it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second version of the discussion, in which the original inference is reversed. This sets up the next step, a challenge to רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the plain reading of 'ובלבד שלא יוציא' is taken to imply only a rabbinic prohibition. That reading now looks like it works against רבא instead of for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces an alternate version of the discussion)
He carried out / moved it beyond

phrases.english: Some say:
this implies: if he carried out, he is exempt but it is forbidden,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the discussion from step 3 with the opposite inference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the inference from the משנה is פטור אבל אסור.

steps.title: Challenge: this would refute רבא
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה implies פטור, it seems to contradict רבא, who rules חייב for carrying four אמות over one's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבא? For רבא said: one who moves an object from the start of four אמות to the end of four אמות, and moved it over his head, is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא, using the second-version inference from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If carrying beyond four אמות at the raised height is only פטור אבל אסור, then the unusual path does reduce liability. That is the opposite of רבא's ruling that passing over one's head does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation
Let it be / shall it be

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rava,
for Rava said:
one who moves (an object) from the beginning of four to the end of four
and moved it over his head, is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 6 to attack רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that carrying four אמות 'דרך עליו' is חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה implies only פטור for carrying at the raised height, the unusual path does lower liability, which contradicts רבא.

steps.title: Rejecting the challenge: maybe it means liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the challenge. The משנה never says פטור אבל אסור; perhaps it means חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it actually teach 'if he carried out he is exempt but it is forbidden'? Perhaps: if he carried out, he is liable to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by showing that the משנה's wording can be read the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 5. Since the משנה does not state the consequence of going beyond four אמות, it may mean חייב חטאת, and then it fits רבא perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (here, at the Torah level)
It teaches (refers to what the משנה actually states)

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the משנה's 'ובלבד שלא יוציא' is ambiguous. It can mean either חייב חטאת or פטור אבל אסור, so it neither proves nor refutes רבא.

phrases.english: Does it teach
'If he carried out, he is exempt but it is forbidden'?
Perhaps: if he carried out —
he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָתָנֵי הוֹצִיא פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge to רבא raised in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The refutation of רבא from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference of פטור אבל אסור is not forced; the משנה may mean חייב חטאת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is ambiguous on this point, so רבא's ruling stands, unproven but not refuted.

steps.title: רב יוסף: urinating or spitting into the public domain makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about standing in a רשות היחיד and urinating or spitting into a רשות הרבים. רב יוסף rules that one who does this is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A person may not stand in a private domain' and urinate or spit into the public domain. רב יוסף said: if he urinated or spat, he is liable to bring a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. רב יוסף then says that urinating or spitting from a רשות היחיד into a רשות הרבים is a full Torah-level violation that requires a קרבן חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says 'לא יעמוד', which means he should not do it. רב יוסף adds that this is not merely a rabbinic prohibition. It counts as real הוצאה (carrying out) and carries full liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Private domain
He urinated
He spat
Liable to bring a sin-offering (a Torah-level violation done unintentionally)
Etc.: the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'A person may not stand in a private domain, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quote of the משנה: he may not urinate or spit into the public domain

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If he urinated or spat, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הִשְׁתִּין וְרָק — חַיָּיב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New section. The גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urinating or spitting from a רשות היחיד into a רשות הרבים makes one חייב חטאת.

steps.title: But there is no four-by-four place for lifting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף. Liability for carrying requires עקירה and הנחה from a place of four by four טפחים, and the mouth or body is not that size.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we require lifting and placing from atop a place of four by four handbreadths, and that is missing here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's ruling. How can there be liability when the spit or urine is not lifted from a proper-sized place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basic rule of הוצאה is that the object must be lifted from, and set down on, a significant place of at least four by four טפחים. A person's mouth or body is far smaller than that. So the עקירה seems to be missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting the object from its place (the start of carrying)
Setting the object down (the end of carrying)
A place of four by four טפחים, the minimum size that counts as significant
And it is not there

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is about the domains. Everyone agrees he moved something from a רשות היחיד to a רשות הרבים. The problem is only the SIZE of the place it came from.

phrases.english: But we require lifting and placing
from atop a place of four by four handbreadths,
and that is missing here!
phrases.notes: The mouth or body is not four by four טפחים

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּעִינַן עֲקִירָה וְהַנָּחָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה, וְלֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling of חייב חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability needs עקירה from a place of four by four טפחים. The mouth or body is too small, so there should be no liability.

steps.title: His intent makes it a significant place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a person's מחשבה (intent) gives the place importance, so it counts as a proper place.
steps.simpleTranslation: His intent makes it a place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in a few words. Because the person considers his mouth or body an important place, it counts as if it were four by four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four-by-four rule is really about whether the place is significant. Physical size is one way to make a place significant. A person's own intent and regard for the place is another.

keyTerms.meaning: His thought or intent
Makes it into a (significant) place

phrases.english: His intent makes it a place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what counts as a מקום ארבעה: intent can stand in for physical size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a place that is physically four by four טפחים counts for עקירה and הנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A place the person regards as significant counts as a מקום ארבעה.

steps.title: Proof from רבא: an object thrown into a dog's mouth or a furnace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that intent makes a place count. רבא rules that throwing an object into a dog's mouth or a furnace's opening makes one liable, even though neither is four by four.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, what about רבא's statement: if one threw an object and it landed in a dog's mouth or in the mouth of a furnace, he is liable to a sin-offering? But we require placing on a place of four by four, and that is missing here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer. Without the idea that intent creates a place, רבא's well-known ruling would make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dog's mouth and a furnace opening are both smaller than four by four, so there is no proper הנחה. Yet רבא still holds him חייב. The only explanation is that the thrower's intent to land it there makes the spot count.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so
He threw
The mouth of a dog
The opening of a furnace or kiln

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then that which Rava said:
if he threw an object and it landed in a dog's mouth
or in the mouth of a furnace, he is liable to a sin-offering,
but we require placing
on top of a place of four by four handbreadths,
and that is missing here!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, הָא דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 11 by showing that רבא's ruling requires it.
steps.raayaObject: The principle מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that throwing into a dog's mouth or a furnace makes one חייב חטאת

steps.title: Intent makes a place, both for רבא's case and for spitting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that intent makes the dog's mouth a place in רבא's case. In the same way, intent makes one's own mouth or body a place in רב יוסף's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his intent makes it a place. Here too, intent makes it a place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by applying the same principle to both cases. רב יוסף's ruling of חייב חטאת stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case, intent supplies the missing הנחה. In רב יוסף's case, intent supplies the missing עקירה. The single principle answers the challenge from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same way
Thought or intent (as a general concept)

steps.whatToRemember: A place smaller than four by four טפחים can still count for עקירה or הנחה if the person's intent makes it significant: מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום. This is why urinating or spitting from a רשות היחיד into a רשות הרבים is חייב חטאת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains how liability for הוצאה can apply to body parts and other small spots that a person deliberately treats as the start or end point of carrying.

phrases.english: Rather, his intent makes it a place;

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי מַחְשָׁבָה מְשַׁוְּיָא לָהּ מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: here too, intent makes it a place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ מְשַׁוְּיָא לֵיהּ מָקוֹם, הָכִי נָמֵי מַחְשָׁבָה מְשַׁוְּיָא לָהּ מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבא's case (step 12) and applies it back to רב יוסף (step 9).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Intent turns a small spot into a significant place, so רב יוסף's ruling of חייב חטאת for urinating or spitting stands.

steps.title: רבא asks: is liability decided by where the urine starts or where it leaves the body?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a person standing in a רשות היחיד whose bodily opening is in the רשות הרבים. Do we judge the transfer by where the urine is uprooted inside the body, or by where it exits?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If a person is in a private domain and the opening of his body is in the public domain, what is the law? Do we go by the place where the urine is uprooted, or by the place where it exits?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds on רב יוסף's ruling and asks about a tricky case: the body is in one domain, but the opening is in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we follow עקירה, the urine is lifted inside the body, which is in the רשות היחיד, and lands in the רשות הרבים. That is a full transfer between domains, so he is liable. If we follow יציאה, the urine only begins its exit at the opening, which is already in the רשות הרבים. Then nothing moved from one domain to another, so there is no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raises a question that has no known answer yet)
The opening of the male organ
We go by the point of uprooting
Exit, the point where it leaves the body
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rava asked:
He is in a private domain
and the opening of his member is in the public domain, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He then urinates.

phrases.english: Do we follow the uprooting,
phrases.notes: The urine is uprooted inside the body, which is in the private domain.

phrases.english: or do we follow the exit?
phrases.notes: The exit happens in the public domain, so there is no transfer between domains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב יוסף's ruling about urinating across domains by testing a borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the transfer judged by where the urine is uprooted inside the body, or by where it physically exits?

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רבא's question is left without an answer: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has no answer to רבא's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means neither side could be proven. The question of עקירה versus יציאה stays open, and the topic closes here.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question remains unresolved.

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the question is silly or rejected. It means it is a real doubt that the גמרא could not decide.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבא's question without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It remains unresolved whether we follow עקירה or יציאה when the body and its opening are in different domains.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה forbid it even if the spittle was not turned over?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about spitting and רבי יהודה's view. It asks whether he forbids walking with spittle even if it was never turned over in the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And likewise one may not spit. רבי יהודה says, etc.' Does this apply even if he did not turn the spittle over in his mouth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה about spitting. It asks a pointed question that sets up a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה in our משנה says that once spittle gathers in the mouth, one may not walk four אמות in the רשות הרבים. That treats the spittle as a separate object being carried. The גמרא asks whether this is true even before the spittle was rolled around in the mouth, which would mean it already counts as detached.

keyTerms.meaning: To spit
Even though
He turned it over, rolled the spittle in his mouth to prepare to spit

phrases.english: And likewise, one may not spit.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says, etc.
phrases.notes: Once spittle gathers in his mouth, he may not walk four אמות until he spits it out.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הַפֵּיךְ בָּהּ?
phrases.english: Even though he did not turn it over?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הַפֵּיךְ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה text to analyze the spitting clause and רבי יהודה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה treat spittle as detached even before it was turned over in the mouth?

steps.title: A משנה shows רבי יהודה holds unturned spittle is not detached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about eating a dried fig with impure hands. There רבי יהודה rules that spittle that was not turned over does not count as a liquid, so it is not considered detached. This contradicts his ruling in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: If someone was eating a dried fig with impure hands and put his hand into his mouth to take out a pebble, רבי מאיר says the fig is impure, and רבי יוסי says it is pure. רבי יהודה says: if he turned the spittle over, the fig is impure; if he did not turn it over, it is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading of רבי יהודה from the previous step. It quotes another משנה where רבי יהודה says unturned spittle is not yet considered separate from the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dry fig can only become impure after a liquid has made it ready for impurity, and the spittle on his hand is that liquid. רבי יהודה says the spittle counts as a liquid only if it was turned over in the mouth. That means unturned spittle is still part of the body. So how can he say in our משנה that walking with unturned spittle counts as carrying an object?

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה (introduces a challenge from a משנה)
A dried fig (here of תרומה)
Impure, unwashed hands (impure by rabbinic law)
A pebble
Rules impure / rules pure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two topics. The fig case is about טומאה, not שבת. The גמרא uses it only to show how רבי יהודה views spittle that was not turned over: it is not yet detached from the body.
steps.whyThisMatters: It forces the גמרא to explain how רבי יהודה can treat unturned spittle as an object for שבת. Steps 18-23 answer this.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
If one was eating a dried fig with impure hands,
and he put his hand into his mouth
to remove a pebble —
Rabbi Meir rules [the fig] impure,
phrases.notes: The spittle made the fig ready to become impure, and then his impure hand made it impure.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei rules it pure.
phrases.notes: Spittle that is still in the mouth does not count as a liquid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he turned it over — impure.
If he did not turn it over — pure!
phrases.notes: So unturned spittle is not considered detached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that turns the previous question into a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רבי יהודה in our משנה, which forbids walking with spittle even if it was not turned over.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the fig משנה, רבי יהודה holds that unturned spittle is not detached from the body. If so, it should not count as a carried object on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The opinions are switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן resolves the contradiction by saying the names in the dried-fig משנה are reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction from Step 17. He says the opinions in the dried-fig משנה were attached to the wrong names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient view in the fig משנה, that unturned spittle is not detached, is not really רבי יהודה's. Once the names are swapped, רבי יהודה holds that spittle in the mouth counts as detached even without being turned over. That matches his ruling in our משנה, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Switched, reversed
The line-up of opinions, meaning which view belongs to which תנא

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not changing our משנה about walking with spittle. He is switching the names in the OTHER משנה, the one about the dried fig and impure hands.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are reversed.
phrases.notes: The names in the dried-fig משנה are swapped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: switching which תנא holds which opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seems to hold in one place that unturned spittle is detached, and in another place that it is not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient fig ruling belongs to a different תנא. רבי יהודה consistently treats spittle in the mouth as detached.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: No switch, our משנה is about phlegm
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש keeps the names as they are and says our משנה is talking about phlegm, not ordinary spittle.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Really, do not switch the opinions. What case are we dealing with here in our משנה? With his phlegm.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש offers a different answer to the same contradiction. He says our משנה is about phlegm (כיח), which is different from ordinary spittle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Phlegm is coughed up from deep inside, so it counts as detached as soon as it reaches the mouth. Ordinary spittle in the mouth is not detached until it is turned over. On this reading, רבי יהודה is consistent and no names need to be switched.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (keeping the original assumption)
Do not switch
What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowing of the case)
His phlegm, the mucus that is coughed up

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Actually, do not reverse the opinions,
and with what are we dealing here?
With his phlegm.
phrases.notes: Our משנה is about phlegm, which is detached right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לָא תַּחְלֵיף, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing answer to the one in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting our משנה to a specific case (phlegm)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to be about ordinary spittle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about phlegm, which is detached once it is in the mouth. Ordinary spittle still needs to be turned over.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say detached spittle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה about something that was 'detached', suggesting it means spittle.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, 'his phlegm, and it was detached.' Isn't it really saying spittle that was detached?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's answer using a ברייתא. It suggests that the ברייתא is really talking about spittle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא proposes that the ברייתא's case, 'his phlegm, and it was detached' (כיחו ונתלש), really refers to spittle that was detached. If the ברייתא is about spittle, then רבי יהודה forbids walking with spittle, and ריש לקיש's limit to phlegm fails.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
Isn't it really saying...? (proposes a reading)
Spittle, ordinary saliva
Was detached, uprooted

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
His phlegm, and it was detached,
is it not really spittle that was detached!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that רבי יהודה's ruling is only about phlegm
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא may really be speaking of spittle that was detached. That would mean רבי יהודה's ruling covers spittle, not only phlegm.

steps.title: No, it really means phlegm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading: the ברייתא means exactly what it says, phlegm that was detached.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means his phlegm that was detached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. The ברייתא is about phlegm, just as it says, so ריש לקיש's answer still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to reinterpret the ברייתא's word 'phlegm' as spittle. Read plainly, the ברייתא supports ריש לקיש's limit to phlegm rather than contradicting it.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejects the proposed reading)

phrases.english: No, it is his phlegm that was detached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed rereading of the ברייתא as being about spittle
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא says phlegm, and there is no reason to read it as spittle.

steps.title: A second ברייתא explicitly mentions spittle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא in which רבי יהודה rules about phlegm AND spittle, which breaks ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, if his phlegm was detached, and likewise if his spittle was detached, he may not walk four אמות until he spits it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge. A different ברייתא says spittle explicitly, side by side with phlegm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'spittle' is written outright, so it cannot be reread as phlegm. This shows that רבי יהודה forbids walking with spittle too, even without turning it over. So limiting our משנה to phlegm cannot solve the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise, the same applies to
Four cubits, the distance that counts as carrying in the רשות הרבים
Until he spits it out

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
His phlegm that was detached,
and likewise his spittle that was detached,
he may not walk four cubits
until he spits it out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge to ריש לקיש after Step 21 deflected the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's limitation of רבי יהודה's ruling to phlegm
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly applies רבי יהודה's prohibition to spittle as well. So the contradiction with the fig משנה returns, and ריש לקיש's answer cannot fix it.

steps.title: Back to the original answer: the opinions are switched
steps.stepSummary: Since ריש לקיש's answer fails, the גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן's answer is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the start: the opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this back-and-forth. It goes back to רבי יוחנן's answer that the names in the fig משנה are reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'phlegm' answer cannot work, because רבי יהודה explicitly includes spittle. The only answer left is רבי יוחנן's: רבי יהודה treats spittle in the mouth as detached, and the lenient view in the fig משנה belongs to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear (the answer that survives)
As we answered at the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה consistently holds that spittle in the mouth counts as detached, even without being turned over. The contradiction is solved by switching the names in the dried-fig משנה (רבי יוחנן). ריש לקיש's 'phlegm' answer is rejected.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes after Step 22 knocked down ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The names in the dried-fig משנה are switched. רבי יהודה holds that spittle in the mouth is detached, consistent with our משנה.

steps.title: Coughing up phlegm in front of one's teacher
steps.stepSummary: Since phlegm came up, the גמרא quotes ריש לקיש: someone who coughs up phlegm before his רבו is liable to death at the hand of Heaven, learned from a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: One who coughs up phlegm in front of his רבו deserves death, as it says, 'All who hate Me love death.' Do not read it as 'those who hate Me' (משנאי), but as 'those who make themselves hated by Me' (משניאי).
steps.whatsHappening: The halachic discussion has ended. The גמרא now adds a related teaching about respect for one's teacher, because the topic of phlegm came up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coughing up phlegm in front of a teacher is a disgusting, disrespectful act. ריש לקיש reads the פסוק with different vowels: instead of 'those who hate Me,' it says 'those who make themselves hateful.' Such people 'love death,' so they are liable to death at the hand of Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Coughed up phlegm
Liable to death (here, at the hand of Heaven)
Do not read it as (a דרשה that rereads the vowels)
Those who make themselves hateful

steps.confusionAlert: 'Do not read it' does not mean the פסוק's text is changed. It is a דרשה that adds a second layer of meaning, while the written פסוק stays the same.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously חז"ל treat כבוד רבו. Even a bodily act done carelessly in front of a teacher counts as a grave offense.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
One who expelled phlegm in front of his teacher
is liable to death,
as it is stated: 'All who hate Me love death' (Proverbs 8:36) —
do not read it as 'those who hate Me,'
but rather 'those who make themselves hateful to Me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כִּיַּח בִּפְנֵי רַבּוֹ חַיָּיב מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected to the sugya by association: the topic of phlegm (כיח).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coughing up phlegm in front of one's רבו is a severe disrespect that makes a person liable to death at the hand of Heaven.

steps.title: But coughing is involuntary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: how can someone deserve מיתה בידי שמים for coughing up phlegm, when a person has no control over that?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is forced! (Nobody coughs on purpose, so why should he be punished?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's harsh statement from the last step. Coughing is not a choice, so how can it be a sin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic rule that a person who acts under compulsion (אונס) is not held responsible. If coughing up phlegm just happens to a person, punishing him with death at the hand of Heaven seems unfair. The גמרא wants to know what kind of case ריש לקיש really means.

keyTerms.meaning: He is completely forced; he cannot help it
Compulsion, something beyond a person's control

phrases.english: But isn't he forced (he can't help it)?
phrases.notes: The doubled verb form (מינס אניס) stresses that he is totally compelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the מימרא of ריש לקיש brought in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that coughing up phlegm before one's רבו makes a person liable to death at the hand of Heaven
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An act done under compulsion carries no guilt, and coughing is involuntary.

steps.title: The case is someone who had phlegm and chose to spit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש does not mean the cough itself. He means someone who had phlegm in his mouth and spat it out in front of his רבו when he could have gone outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about someone who had phlegm and spat it out (in front of his teacher, when he could have stepped away).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the punishment is not for the cough. It is for choosing to spit in front of his רבו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phlegm coming up is beyond his control, but spitting it out right there is a choice. He could have left his רבו's presence and spat outside. That choice shows disrespect, so the punishment is not for an act of אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought up phlegm
And he spat
We are saying, we are talking about

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's harsh punishment applies only to the voluntary part, spitting in front of the רבו, not to the involuntary cough.

phrases.english: We are speaking of one who had phlegm and spat it out.
phrases.notes: In other words, he had time to step away and spit outside but did it in front of his רבו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a voluntary act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The punishment seemed to be for the involuntary cough itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The punishment is for choosing to spit in front of his רבו instead of going outside.

steps.title: New משנה: drinking from one domain into another
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that on שבת a person may not stand in one domain and drink in the other unless his head and most of his body are inside the domain where he drinks. The same rule applies at a winepress.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not stand in a private domain and drink in a public domain, or stand in a public domain and drink in a private domain, unless he puts his head and most of his body into the place where he is drinking. The same applies at a winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion of phlegm is over, and a new משנה begins. It sets a rule about drinking across the boundary between רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that he might pull the drink or the cup over to himself and carry it from one domain into another. If his head and most of his body are already in the domain where the drink is, the problem goes away. The phrase "the same at a winepress" will be explained by the גמרא later.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Private domain
Public domain
His head and most of his body
Winepress

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה opens with "לֹא יַעֲמוֹד", meaning a person may NOT stand this way. The permission comes only through "אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן", when his head and most of his body are inside.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may not stand in a private domain
and drink in a public domain,
or stand in a public domain and drink in a private domain,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִכְנִיס רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ
phrases.english: unless he brought his head and most of his body
into the place where he is drinking.
And the same applies at a winepress.
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains this later.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְיִשְׁתֶּה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the discussion of phlegm.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may drink from another domain only if his head and most of his body are inside the domain where he drinks.

steps.title: The previous משנה follows the רבנן, but this one follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The previous משנה matches the רבנן, who let a person in one domain handle objects in another domain. This משנה forbids that, which matches רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part (the previous משנה) follows the רבנן, and the later part (this משנה) follows רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that two neighboring משניות seem to follow opposite opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה allowed a person standing in one domain to move objects in the other domain, which is the view of the רבנן. Our משנה forbids drinking from another domain unless he goes inside, which sounds like רבי מאיר's stricter view. Normally we expect neighboring משניות to follow one consistent opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part (here, the previous משנה)
The latter part (here, this משנה)
The Sages, the majority opinion
A תנא who is stricter in this matter

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The first clause follows the Rabbis,
and the latter clause follows Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה of step 27 by comparing it to the previous משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of our משנה with the previous משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neighboring משניות should follow one opinion, but the previous one allows handling objects in another domain (רבנן) while this one forbids it (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: רב יוסף: objects one needs, and everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that our משנה deals with objects the person needs. For such objects even the רבנן agree that he must not handle them across domains, because he might pull them over to himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Our משנה is about objects that he needs, and here everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by showing that the two משניות deal with different kinds of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן allow handling objects in another domain only when the person does not especially need them. When he needs the object, like a drink he wants, there is a real worry that he will absent-mindedly draw it over to his own domain and break an איסור תורה. So in this case even the רבנן agree with the stricter rule, and the two משניות do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer
Objects that he needs
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: Even the lenient רבנן forbid handling something across domains when the person needs it, because he may pull it over to himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a lenient opinion can still have limits. The leniency of the רבנן does not cover cases where the person is likely to bring the object into his own domain.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is about objects that he needs,
and it is the view of everyone.
phrases.notes: The worry is that he will draw the object over to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בַּחֲפֵיצִין שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לוֹ, וְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (objects one needs versus objects one does not need)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to follow רבי מאיר alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה deals with objects one needs, where even the רבנן forbid handling them across domains, so it is the view of everyone.

steps.title: What is the law if one area is a כרמלית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's rule about drinking across domains also applies when one of the areas is a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what about a כרמלית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question. The משנה forbade drinking across רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים, and now we ask whether the same applies to a כרמלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case involved two domains defined by Torah law. A כרמלית is an in-between area, like a field or the sea, that the חכמים treated as a domain. The question is whether the protective rule from the משנה also reaches this rabbinic domain.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (the חכמים)
An in-between area, neither fully private nor fully public, whose carrying ban is rabbinic
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
A karmelit, what is the law?
phrases.notes: If one of the two areas in the משנה's case is a כרמלית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's rule (Step 27), as explained by רב יוסף (Step 29), to a new kind of domain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on drinking across domains apply when one of the domains is a כרמלית?

steps.title: אביי: A כרמלית follows the same rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a כרמלית has the same law as the Torah-level domains in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that a כרמלית is treated just like the domains in the משנה, so you may not drink across it either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's view, the worry from רב יוסף (that the person might pull the object over to himself) applies equally when one side is a כרמלית. So the protective rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the same thing (same law)
Private domain (Torah-level)
Public domain (Torah-level)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This is the same as that.
phrases.notes: A כרמלית follows the same rule as a Torah-level domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban applies to a כרמלית as well.

steps.title: רבא: We do not make a decree on top of a decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the ban on carrying in a כרמלית is itself only a rabbinic decree, so we should not add another decree to protect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The כרמלית itself is a decree. Should we then go and make a decree to protect a decree?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues against אביי. He says the כרמלית should not be included in the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on drinking across domains is a safeguard, a גזירה, against actually moving the object. With a כרמלית, moving the object is itself forbidden only by the חכמים. A safeguard for a safeguard is a גזירה לגזירה, which the חכמים normally do not make.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
A decree to protect another decree, which is normally not made
Of rabbinic (not Torah) origin

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say that carrying into a כרמלית is allowed. It is still forbidden. He only says we do not add the extra fence of not drinking across it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle that we do not make a גזירה לגזירה comes up all over ש״ס as a limit on rabbinic decrees.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It [the karmelit] itself is a decree,
and shall we rise up and decree
phrases.notes: Said as a rhetorical question.

phrases.english: a decree to protect a decree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא גּוּפָא גְּזֵירָה, וַאֲנַן נֵיקוּם וְנִגְזוֹר גְּזֵירָה לִגְזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's answer in Step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that a כרמלית follows the משנה's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the כרמלית ban is already a גזירה, including it would make a גזירה לגזירה, which the חכמים do not do.

steps.title: אביי begins his proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens a proof for his view by pointing to the wording of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From where do I say this? From what the משנה teaches...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. אביי is getting ready to quote words from the משנה to show that it includes a כרמלית. The quote itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי answers רבא's challenge by turning to the text of the משנה. He will argue that one of its cases can only be about a כרמלית, which would prove that the rule does apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (introducing a source)
From the fact that it teaches (in the משנה)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From where do I say it?
From the fact that it teaches
phrases.notes: The quoted משנה text continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's objection, אביי defends his own view from Step 31 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that the rule applies to a כרמלית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה (Step 27), quoted on the next amud
